global_organization_chain: Summary compresses industry risk, three-model architecture, terminal location, bankruptcy timing, strategy regimes, and validation claims.
Introduction, problem reconstruction, assumptions, and overview route official requirements into forecast, migration, and company outputs.
Data preparation turns April-July temperatures and a spherical domain into annual valid projected fields.
ARIMA fitting, order selection, and residual simulation produce future temperature fields.
Temperature gradients, a shared thermal gate, and annual particle advection produce terminal location maps.
Distance cost, density/freshness income, and profit translate migration into operating-time distributions.
Port relocation and refrigeration/territorial masks create two management scenarios.
Sensitivity, Q-Q robustness, problem-indexed conclusion, sparse references, public article, and code appendices close the evidence chain.

main_argument_chains.claim: Historical temperature fields can support a 50-year probabilistic ocean forecast.
support_steps: Select an order by blocked RMSE.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Supply uncertainty-aware habitat fields only after forward hindcasts and covariance regularization.

main_argument_chains.claim: Temperature change can be converted into northward fish displacement.
support_steps: Apply a thermal gate and saturating speed.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Produce separate herring and mackerel distributions after calibration to observed species trajectories and mass conservation.

warnings.warning: The April-July seasonal mean is not justified for both herring and mackerel life cycles or migration seasons.
A partial seasonal mean uses fewer months without weighting or uncertainty, so years are not directly comparable.
Linear interpolation across missing years is treated as observed temperature and its uncertainty is not propagated.
The four-missing-year threshold is arbitrary and receives no sensitivity analysis.
A data-invalid grid column is declared physically unreachable, conflating missingness with land or habitat barriers.
The exact map projection and forward/inverse equations are absent, so the distance transformation cannot be independently reproduced from the report.
No maximum or spatial distribution of projection distortion is reported across the 25-degree-latitude by 35-degree-longitude domain.
The dense Figure 5 spaghetti plot does not establish the stated absence of trend or the stationarity needed for ARIMA differencing.
The report says vector autoregression considers spatial-temporal correlation, but Equation (2) and fitAR estimate each grid cell's mean dynamics independently.
Equation (2) has no intercept, but fitAR adds a p+1 design column and simulate adds the fitted inception every year; this undeclared term can drive long-horizon drift.
Only 60 annual seasonal observations support a 50-year recursive extrapolation, with no long-horizon hindcast.
The model omits explicit trend, climate forcing, seasonality beyond aggregation, ocean circulation, and exogenous variables despite a climate-change task.
Equation (3) is written as an expectation of past expected differences without a clearly defined conditional information set.
Equation (4) accumulates residual shocks through an integrated process, but no fan chart or forecast-variance growth is reported.
Normal residuals are assumed without residual normality, autocorrelation, heteroskedasticity, or spatial-dependence diagnostics.
The Summary calls the source monthly data while the fitted series are annual April-July means; the effective modeling frequency is not stated consistently.
The Summary calls the data global, but the report and code restrict the fitted domain to 50-75 N and 25 W-10 E.
The normal equations are shown without rank or condition checks for the differenced lag design.
Directly forming and inverting X^T X is numerically less stable than QR/SVD or a linear solve and no conditioning error is assessed.
Grid-specific coefficient estimates and their uncertainty are never reported, preventing forecast reproduction from the paper alone.
The six folds are not forward-chaining: most held-out decades are forecast using training observations from later years, causing temporal leakage.

The crossvalidation function calls forecast on the held-out decade itself, so its lag inputs and differencing anchors come from test observations rather than a recursive forecast from the training endpoint.
Pooling one-step or block errors across 690 cells does not validate a recursive 50-year forecast horizon.
Only four ARIMA(p,d,0) choices are compared; moving-average terms, drift, trend, seasonal structure, and spatial benchmarks are excluded.
Figure 6 gives boxplots but no numeric fold RMSE table, baseline model, or significance of the small difference between candidates.
A 690-by-690 residual covariance estimated from roughly 59 residual years has rank at most about 58 and is not identifiable without regularization.
Drawing multivariate-normal residuals is parametric Monte Carlo, not bootstrap resampling as repeatedly claimed.
The published code sets bs=false, which sets N_sim=1 rather than 10,000.
With bs=false the random residual term is multiplied by zero, so the published execution path is deterministic.
The code uses rng('default'), but the paper never states the actual switch, seed, or saved ensemble used for the reported probabilities.
simulate is called with 2070-2018+1 ticks; the exact mapping of seed years, returned years, and the advertised 50-year horizon is not documented.
The appendix omits sst.mean.nc and helper dependencies such as readnc, getsst, geodetic2cartesian, and landclear, and several printed code lines are clipped at the right margin.
The printed x finite difference divides by dt instead of dx and also changes both space and future time, so it is not partial u/partial x.
The printed y finite difference divides by dt instead of dy and also changes both space and future time, so it is not partial u/partial y.
The appendix code correctly divides spatial differences by coordinate differences, materially disagreeing with printed Equation (11).
No grid-refinement or interpolation-error test supports the numerical gradient driving all fish movement.
Beta is reported without units even though it is added to a temperature-gradient norm and therefore must share degree-C-per-distance units.
vmax=188.5671 km/year is described as estimated from migration data, but code sets it to 2.5 times mean grid spacing.
beta is described as an empirical migration coefficient, but code sets it to the median historical temperature-gradient magnitude.
The code-only gate makes fish motion exactly zero whenever temperature is between 2 and 6 C, a decisive behavior absent from the displayed notation.
Herring and mackerel are assigned the same 2-6 C preferred interval, speed, and response despite distinct ecology.
Temperature alone determines migration; currents, prey, salinity, spawning, depth, density, age, and species interactions are omitted.
The normalized-gradient law fixes direction but does not calibrate observed displacement trajectories or migration timing.
The code initializes one equal particle at every valid ocean grid cell rather than using observed herring or mackerel distributions.
No data or state distinguishes the two target species, so all location maps are for one synthetic particle field.
A one-year advection step receives no step-size or integration-convergence test.
Invalid or land-crossing trial velocities are set to zero, which can create artificial coastal and boundary accumulation.
The model has no mass-conservation equation, particle weights, births, deaths, diffusion, or density reconstruction method.
Algorithm 1 says fish density is refreshed, but Equation (8) and code update only particle coordinates.
The cost model freezes fuel prices, wages, maintenance, vessel technology, and macroeconomics for 50 years.
Trip cost omits fishing effort, travel time, catch duration, crew scheduling, capacity, quota, and weather risk.
C0=1616 USD and a=3.01 USD/km are attributed only to broad FAO investigation, without sample rows or conversion.
Normalized rho has no unit or calibration to tonnes, catch-per-unit-effort, or separate species abundance.
The income coefficient theta conflates catchability, vessel capacity, fish price, effort, and market demand.
Freshness decay is modeled against distance, although spoilage and price depend on time, temperature, handling, and species.
Table 4 reports lambda in year/km, but the exponent lambda*d is dimensionless only if lambda has units 1/km.
Equation (15) is labeled fishing profit P in prose but prints I(x,y) on the left, reusing the income symbol.
The paper never defines how site-level or per-particle profit is aggregated to one company's annual profit.
Algorithm 2 says profit is evaluated for each single fish, but Equation (15) contains fixed cost C0; a literal per-particle or per-cell application would subtract the fixed trip cost repeatedly.
Bankruptcy is not defined in terms of cash reserve, capital, debt, repeated losses, or assets; it appears to be inferred from nonpositive modeled profit.
The appendix publishes no Model III profit, aggregation, bankruptcy, relocation, refrigeration, or territorial-water code.
The reported 2030, 2039, and 2070 times therefore cannot be reproduced from the disclosed code.
Calling 2030 worst, 2070 best, and 2039 most likely mixes sampled extrema, censoring, and a modal point mass without interval definitions.
The Summary treats 0.02%, 8.25%, and 5.27% as probabilities of worst, most likely, and best cases, though they are point/censoring masses in a time histogram.
Under the claimed 10,000 paths, 0.02% represents only two paths and the paper reports no binomial or simulation uncertainty interval for any bankruptcy or strategy percentage.
The reported percentages describe frequencies across simulated climate-migration paths, not survival fractions across an identified population of heterogeneous fishing companies.
The official 'too far away' threshold is replaced by an undocumented bankruptcy proxy, without species-specific distance limits or elapsed-time definitions.
The vessel sample size N and individual maximum-range observations used to obtain L=1000 km are absent.
Setting price to exactly half at the average maximum range is an assumption, not a fitted freshness-price relationship.
C_mean and P_mean are called averages but their printed definitions are spatial sums without normalization.
C_mean=4,040,000 USD is inconsistent in scale with the per-trip C0 and distance cost unless it is an aggregate, but the aggregation domain is not reported.
theta=9440.73 has no clearly closed unit because rho and P_mean are undefined normalized aggregates.
The financial data source is a homepage-level FAO reference rather than a traceable company sample, year, currency conversion, or dataset.
The Iceland relocation scenario changes distance but omits purchase/lease, port fees, taxes, labor relocation, permits, and asset constraints.
A 100 percent survival claim from an uncosted port move is not evidence that the strategy is practical or economically attractive for limited-capital firms.
The territorial scenario excludes Icelandic and Norwegian blocks wholesale instead of varying the official 'some proportion of the fishery' input.
The territorial mask is not derived from the official 12-nautical-mile definition with a published geospatial procedure.
The roughly one-degree ocean grid is coarser than a 12-nautical-mile territorial sea, so whole-block exclusion cannot resolve the legal boundary it claims to model.

The forecast peak is described as lying between Iceland and the Faroe Islands, yet the access scenario discusses only Icelandic and Norwegian blocks and does not address Faroese or Danish jurisdiction.
The refrigeration scenario provides no new lambda, equipment cost, fuel/maintenance cost, vessel capacity, financing, or installation schedule.
The conclusion says improved ship technology has a higher cost, but that cost is absent from the strategy profit equation.
The Problem 4 conclusion first prescribes refrigeration because the port cannot move, then says 62.68 percent survive 'if the departure ports are changed,' contradicting its own scenario definition.
The scenarios move the representative port or refrigerate the fleet wholesale; no decision variable represents the requested fraction of assets or vessels to relocate or upgrade.
Foreign access, quota, licensing, innocent passage versus fishing rights, and bilateral policy are reduced to a binary no-entry assumption.
The second printed finite difference uses eta(r+Delta L)-eta(L), mixing the profit-margin and range variables.
The paper does not state Delta r or Delta L, simulation repeats, or uncertainty bands for sensitivity slopes.
Only two economic factors are varied; the far more uncertain forecast, covariance, thermal thresholds, speed, costs, and legal access are omitted.
Higher r mechanically increases calibrated theta and survival, so the monotone result is partly built into Equation (18).
Increasing navigation range is interpreted as purely beneficial even though fuel, travel time, freshness loss, and capital cost should also rise.
Agreement with intuition is a sanity check and does not prove rationality or robustness against observed company outcomes.
Figure 15's survival curves are not reconciled with the reported 5.27 percent baseline, 62.68 percent refrigeration, or 100 percent relocation outcomes, so the sensitivity scenario is ambiguous.
No initial-distribution generator, number of samples, species constraints, or terminal RMSE table is reported.
Pairwise RMSE values reuse simulations and are not independent observations for a standard Q-Q interpretation.
A straight Q-Q plot suggests an approximately normal RMSE distribution, not that RMSE magnitudes are small.
Figure 16's upper tail visibly bends away from the reference line, so even the claimed approximate normal shape is not uniformly supported.
No acceptance threshold, baseline scale, confidence interval, or decision comparison defines 'similar final distribution'.
The Q-Q shape cannot verify the decisive role of temperature because no competing migration mechanisms are fitted or ablated.
Figure 16's RMSE quantiles are positive and roughly 2.7-4.0, but the field scale and practical meaning are not explained.
The required magazine article repeats the disputed 10,000-run probabilities without explaining the bankruptcy event or code discrepancy.
The article recommends general industry participation, larger navigation radius, and low-carbon behavior rather than clearly explaining the modeled relocation/refrigeration choices.
The article's fish banner and port map have no visible source citation, despite the official unauthorized-image warning.
The article cites an IPCC fifth-report warming claim and more-than-one-degree rise since 1870 without a reference entry or mapping to the modeled dataset.
Only five references are provided and none trace the exact temperature, fish distribution, financial, vessel, projection, ARIMA, territorial, or image data used.
Every page contains an orange third-party MATHmodels QR watermark that is not part of the original team submission.
